boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on Oxford’s Courthouse Square, North Lamar Boulevard, Van Buren Avenue, and University Avenue—within the practical orbit of the University of Mississippi.

cards.title: Browse author-event shelves
cards.subtitle: 160 Courthouse Square · Courthouse Square corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Courthouse Square corridor to Square Books, then check its event information before choosing a book or planning an author-program visit.
cards.short_summary: Independent bookstore with a documented author-events program.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford identifies Square Books at 160 Courthouse Square and says it hosts more than 150 author events annually.
cards.access_notes: Retail bookstore; confirm event details and any ticket requirements with the venue.

cards.title: Find youth and YA reads
cards.subtitle: 111 Courthouse Square · Courthouse Square corridor
cards.notes: Use the Courthouse Square corridor to reach Square Books Jr. and browse its children’s, middle-grade, and young-adult book selection.
cards.short_summary: A children’s and young-adult bookstore on the Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford lists Square Books Jr. at 111 Courthouse Square and describes books for children and young teens plus educational toys and games.

cards.title: Look for collectible editions
cards.subtitle: 115 Courthouse Square · Courthouse Square corridor
cards.notes: Head to 115 Courthouse Square and browse the specialty stock of collectible, vintage, and first-edition books at Rare Square Books.
cards.short_summary: Specialty book destination for collectible and vintage editions.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford places Rare Square Books at 115 Courthouse Square and describes collectible, vintage, and first-edition books.
cards.access_notes: Located above Square Books Jr.; verify current access before visiting.

cards.title: Check the Southern-lit selection
cards.subtitle: 129 Courthouse Square · Courthouse Square corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 129 Courthouse Square to browse new releases and Southern literature; review the bookstore’s calendar if you want an author event.
cards.short_summary: Independent bookstore with Southern literature and author events.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford lists Off Square Books at 129 Courthouse Square and describes new releases, Southern literature, and author events.
cards.access_notes: Retail bookstore; event access and purchases may vary.

cards.title: See the current gallery work
cards.subtitle: 150 Courthouse Square · Courthouse Square corridor
cards.notes: Walk to 150 Courthouse Square and look for the current exhibition; the gallery documents work by regional, national, and international artists.
cards.short_summary: Art gallery presenting work from multiple geographic scopes.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford identifies Southside Gallery at 150 Courthouse Square and says it showcases regional, national, and international artwork.
cards.access_notes: Check the gallery directly for exhibition dates and entry details.

cards.title: Tour the Square’s focal point
cards.subtitle: Courthouse Square · Courthouse Square corridor
cards.notes: Use the courthouse as a walking anchor for the Square corridor, then ask locally about touring the 1872 building and its public access.
cards.short_summary: Historic courthouse at the center of Oxford’s Square.
cards.evidence_claim: The Oxford Lafayette Chamber identifies the Historic Oxford Courthouse as the Square’s focal point, built in 1872, and says visitors may tour it.
cards.source_title: Historic Oxford Square | Oxford Lafayette Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: Tour availability may change; verify access with the relevant local office.

cards.title: Choose a small-batch scoop
cards.subtitle: 309 North Lamar · North Lamar Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Follow North Lamar Boulevard to Oxford Creamery for its documented small-batch, Southern-style ice cream made with locally sourced ingredients.
cards.short_summary: Ice-cream stop on North Lamar Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford lists Oxford Creamery at 309 North Lamar and describes small-batch Southern-style ice cream made from scratch.
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required to order; verify current hours directly.

cards.title: Browse breads and pastries
cards.subtitle: 923 Van Buren Avenue · Van Buren Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Van Buren Avenue corridor to Bottletree Bakery and choose from its documented scratch-made breads, pastries, and specialty coffee.
cards.short_summary: Bakery and café serving scratch-made breads and pastries.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford lists Bottletree Bakery at 923 Van Buren Avenue and describes scratch-made European-style breads, pastries, and specialty coffee.
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required to order; verify current hours directly.

cards.title: Look for an arts event
cards.subtitle: University Avenue · University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Take University Avenue to the Powerhouse Community Arts Center and consult its program for arts events or exhibits during your visit.
cards.short_summary: Community arts center near the Square with events and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford says the Powerhouse Community Arts Center is on University Avenue, a short walk from the Square, and hosts arts events and exhibits.
cards.access_notes: The source lists weekday daytime hours; confirm the current event schedule before going.

cards.title: Pick up Square orientation
cards.subtitle: 107 Courthouse Square · Courthouse Square corridor
cards.notes: Start at 107 Courthouse Square to request visitor guidance, then use the information desk to orient yourself along the surrounding Square corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Oxford lists its Welcome Center at 107 Courthouse Square and states that visitors may drop by for assistance.
cards.access_notes: The source lists weekday and Saturday visitor-center hours; confirm before visiting.
